In Surgeon Simulator 2013 you control Nigel Burke, a guy who can't even tie his shoe laces without making "finger spaghetti" out of himself. Anyway, you control his fingers and thumb using the keyboard, which works well at simulating a hand. The controls can get a little frustrating, however I think that was a little on purpose. Now, most of you are all wondering the same question: Does it have a good story? Yes. It shows a man who poses a lack of hand motor skills and has a dream of becoming a surgeon, the best surgeon, but you are the only one who can fulfil his dream.
 The story and game play intertwine nicely and always makes you ask the same question: Was it worth it? As you stare down at the life insurance fee, was it worth it...? That aside, the game has three different types of surgery: Heart Transplant, Kidney Transplant and the Brain Transplant. They all are extremely fun and varied and include funny references, while you Tomahawk Chop someone in the skull. There is also a few secret levels, which I won't tell you about since they are...secret. Just go easy on the heavy (I've given my condolences to enough Team Fortress characters). 

In a nutshell, Surgeon Simulator controls well,  Has frustratingly-fun levels and even the starting menu provided for several minutes of fun.

[b] NOTE: [/b] This is my first review, so I know it isn't that good, however I hope to get better as I write more.

Long spoken of as myth, fairy-tale or merely the raving delusions of a mad man, an ancient and mysterious evil has awoken and proven itself a very real and dangerous threat to all in the once pleasant land of Infirmary. But there is yet hope as a band of unlikely heroes unite to vanquish this foe and send it back to the vile domain from whence it came. Play the roles of plucky Pinkie, the young but eager son of a blacksmith, Ring, the exiled princess trying to win back her rightful place as heir to the throne, the short-tempered Middle with a past shrouded in secrecy and an apparent score to settle, Thumb, the stoic and noble paladin sworn to defend the realm, and their brave leader Index, who together form the brotherhood of The Hand of Nigel, as they set forth on adventure in a world filled with peril at every turn.
 
Face hideous, demented foes throughout the course of your journey such as the snake-like Intesties, the oozing Liveros, and the worst villains of them all, The Board of Medical Examiners. Lay siege to their fortress of bones, but choose your weapons careful, as only the right tools will grant you access to their grotesque dungeons. Mere tiny blades and cutting devices will ne'er be enough to pass, but with steadfast determination and a mighty hammer you will see your way through to the inner sanctum. Once inside be prepared to face the horrible wretches that lie in wait for you, the bosses within the bowels of each twisted lair, including Master Pump, The Piss-taker, and the most sickening of them all... Big Brain. Only when these are vanquished will you truly be able to call yourself the Hero of Infirmary and claim the hand of the fair maiden Trisha.
 
It is not a quest for those faint of heart or lacking in skill or valour, but great rewards await any warrior brave enough to take on this challenge as you traverse the wastelands, do battle astride the back of high speed carriages, and even magically voyage through the cold, dark void of outer space on your intrepid excursions. Find glory and pass into legend, or succumb to the forces of evil and meet your doom, but whatever you do, tread carefully lest you summon the wrath of the greatest danger of all, the all-knowing, omnipresent... Bob.

Surgeon Simulator is a first person QWOP game. You take the role of a surgeon named Nigel Burke. Mouse movements control your doctor’s hand, up, down, left, right, and rotating. A, W, E, R and space bar are all used to control individual fingers on the hand, this is used to grasp the utensils, The game play consists of the player trying to complete a number of different operations on your patient, the first being something as simple as a heart transplant. 

Once completing the first operations, you then unlock different scenarios, such as ambulance operations, ad space operations, which incorporate bumping round tools and zero gravity, 

The graphics are nicely presented and everything looks clean and polished, I don't think photo realism graphics would be something I would be looking for in this type of game anyway. The soundtrack is mainly the general hospital/emergency theme tune the whole time, I had to turn it off after the first hour or two as it just grew very repetitive very fast, all of the sound effects in game of the grinding, sawing and squelching are all very nicely produced. 

This game is hard, like, hard as nails hard, I am nowhere near completing it, and I have played for almost eleven hours, your hands start to ache if you play any more than an hour due to the intense holding down of the buttons and thought that goes into picking up a single item, it is unbelievable, I did try out using a controller using Pinnacle Gaming Profile (quick shout out to them while I am at it), and this did make the controls a little easier to use, but it was still stupidly difficult.

I haven't found any technical issues, I would think a potato could run Surgeon Simulator; it's a well optimized game.

A lot of the time I spent on this was playing with friends, just playing around seeing how messed up we could get, and that's what this game is all about, just having a laugh and giggle, it's hard to sit down on your own for hours at a time on this game just because of how strenuous it is on your hand and thought process just to pick something up. But I do recommend that people pick it up, just for the novelty value and for some couch gaming with friends.

Intro:

Ask anybody that owns it about why they bought the game and they will most likley say "Because it looked funny". I mean, who really want's to buy this for the pure challenge of preforming sugery on a patient? I would assume you want to buy this as an escape from the daily life, to the inner realms of video games where everything that happens is supposed to be a fun experience, and I think it does this fairly well.

Gameplay:

I think that the gameplay is pretty hard, and the fact that it is hard is just the point of the game. The devs as gamers thought about the most annoying things you could implement, and afterward implemented them. I think that the devs never expected this to be a really good game that people played and speedran just due to the fact that it was only intended as a quick laugh and nothing more. When it comes to the Pros and the Cons of the game I don't like adressing them just due to the fact that as previously stated, the cons were intended for the end product long before the release of the game. I can't judge the gameplay of this as it really depends on your sense of humor and expectations of what a game should be.

Conclusion:

Since this game was mainly to make a funny statement about something, I don't feel like you should even consider playing it like a real video game, but to play it as a form of comedy that you may come back to after a hard day of work. To actually play it as a fully fledged video game is just foolhardy, and if you want a FAIR challenging experience, I wouldn't really recommend it in any way shape or form. 100%ing this thing was really pointless in the whole scheme of things, and in all honesty it ruined the experience of ever playing a game like it again. I think if it's on sale (which it usally is) go for it, there is no crime in laughing at a fake man's misery, or doing psychologically questionable things to his organs, however, I urge you to never ever play it like a real game, but to only ever play it as a silly satire on the "Simulation" genre of today...

The character models and environments are stylized, contributing to the game's comedic atmosphere. While not graphically demanding, the intentionally chaotic aesthetics suit the nature of the gameplay.

Gameplay: ★★★★☆
The gameplay in Surgeon Simulator is intentionally wacky and challenging. Controlling the surgeon's hand, players perform surgeries using deliberately awkward controls, leading to hilariously unpredictable outcomes. The sheer absurdity and frustration of the controls contribute to the game's charm, offering a unique and comical take on the simulation genre.

Story: ★★☆☆☆
Surgeon Simulator doesn't emphasize narrative, and the story takes a backseat to the chaotic surgical scenarios. The primary focus is on the absurdity of performing surgeries with intentionally difficult controls. While there's a loose premise involving surgeries and various environments, the narrative isn't a significant aspect of the experience.

Soundtrack: ★★★☆☆

The level design adds variety to the challenges, requiring players to adapt their surgical skills to different environments. The intentionally exaggerated and humorous elements enhance the overall experience.

Replayability: ★★★☆☆
Surgeon Simulator's replay value lies in its absurdity and the enjoyment derived from experimenting with unconventional surgeries. The intentionally difficult controls and unpredictable outcomes encourage players to revisit surgeries for laughs and share their chaotic experiences with others. Overall: ★★★☆☆
Surgeon Simulator delivers a unique and comical take on the simulation genre. Its intentionally awkward controls, chaotic surgical scenarios, and humorous atmosphere make it an entertaining and memorable experience. While it may not offer deep storytelling or complex gameplay mechanics, the game's charm lies in its ability to induce laughter through surgical mishaps and absurdity.

Developed by Bossa Studios and released on steam in 2013, Surgeon Simulator is a combination of a physics centric and simulation of sorts with controls that are intentionally floaty. 

As the name of the game suggests, you play as a surgeon performing different surgeries in different places and your main objective is to keep the patients alive. The main challenge comes from the blood loss, that acts as constant countdown (but there are ways to slow it down) but the different locations present other hurdles to overcome, like a constantly moving ambulance. 

The surgeries are taken in a comedic tone, and you can use all tools available, from traditional scalpels, bone saws, and even hammers in an effort to decrease blood loss and time spent in each surgery. 

There are many secrets and fun things to do, other than the surgeries, most are hinted by the achievements, that can act as a guide finding these special activities. 

Controlled using the keyboard and mouse, you can rebind the keys, but that won’t remove the floaty controls, which are intentionally made. The keyboard controls the opening and closing of fingers, while the mouse controls the hand movement, the left button the lowering of the hand and the right button the rotation of the hand. In a way this game is like a twisted claw machine, with organs and tools. 

Although this game doesn’t allow for online multiplayer, with a friend in the same room this game is an amazing experience. No bigger fun than laughing together from failed attempts blaming the controls, until those just start to make sense, and the surgery changes and the cycle starts over. 

Either way, alone or with a friend, this game has a lot to offer so I can easilly recommend it.

[h1] Yeeting Medical Equipment Simulator [/h1]

Surgeon Simulator is a physics-based "rage game" where you take control of a hand with flimsy controls as you attempt to extract organs from people. The "main appeal" of the game is obviously its physics, as the hand you control is designed to be difficult to control. You'll be flailing the hand around as you attempt to grab surgery equipment, moving each finger individually, and cut people open to extract and replace the organs. The levels vary between various surgeries, with most being the same concept and are fairly straight forward. You have to extract the organs, but prevent blood loss otherwise you'll lose. To do so, you have to frequently stab the patient anywhere with the green needle. Once you complete the basic levels, the game will add new challenges like riding in an ambulance or performing in zero-G. Your enjoyment of the game will entirely depend on how much you like the "funny frustration games", you'll have trouble managing the controls as you fiddle around with the equipment and eventually try to repeat the same moves over and over again. You'll become irritated as the environment suddenly bounces your favorite equipment off and you may even have to end up restarting.

Still, the controls aren't entirely unfair. After a while you'll get the hang of it and realize the monotony of the game. There will become no challenge, and the "rage" will just be annoyance as some things happen without your intervention. Even if you perfect the controls, there are still heavy limitations of the game. You'll find your hand unable to reach certain areas to even grab the organs sometimes, or unable to properly grasp a tool because it keeps flipping around. The actual surgery is arbitrary, as the green needle will completely stop bleeding and therefore it's more of a nuisance than an actual challenge, where the real challenge is losing your tools. Although the levels try to add variety, they're literally the same procedure just with more annoyances and really once you do the first round of them you might already become bored with the game. I feel like this game is divisive, as those who want a "real game" are going to be unsatisfied, but those who want to "silly physics" and don't mind losing may be satisfied. Overall, I personally wouldn't recommend it, but for its price and maybe "niche" audience you could try giving it a shot. 

[h1]Pros: [/h1]
[list]
[*]The controls are hard, but it is possible to master them

[*]Unexpected situations can lead to some intense moments as you scramble for certain tools to prevent a loss
